Facilities Manager – Data Center

The Facilities Manager leads a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians, contractors, and service providers responsible for maintaining highly available, mission-critical data center infrastructure.
This position oversees daily facilities operations, maintenance programs, capital projects, vendor performance, safety, compliance, and operational risk. The Facilities Manager drives operational excellence through continuous improvement, sustainability initiatives, strong technical governance, and proactive asset management.

Critical Facilities Operations
Lead the day-to-day operation of all critical data center infrastructure.
Ensure the availability and reliability of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, security, and life-safety systems.
Maintain compliance with Service Level Agreements, operational standards, and uptime objectives.
Oversee 24/7 operational support, including incident response, escalation, and recovery.
Ensure Standard Operating Procedures, Emergency Operating Procedures, and Methods of Procedure are accurate, current, and consistently followed.
Review and approve high-risk maintenance activities and changes affecting critical infrastructure.
Support capacity planning and ensure infrastructure can meet current and future operational requirements.
Leadership and Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop Critical Facilities Engineers and Technicians.
Manage shift schedules, staffing levels, technical training, competency assessments, and performance evaluations.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and development plans.
Foster a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.
Coordinate contractor and vendor activities to ensure work is completed safely, on time, and to the required quality standards.
Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention of facilities personnel.
Maintenance and Asset Management
Develop and oversee preventive, predictive, condition-based, and corrective maintenance programs.
Manage maintenance planning, scheduling, work orders, and equipment records through the Computerized Maintenance Management System.
Ensure maintenance activities are properly risk-assessed, documented, approved, and communicated.
Monitor equipment condition and lifecycle performance and develop repair, upgrade, and replacement strategies.
Ensure maintenance activities minimize operational risk, service disruption, and unplanned downtime.
Review recurring equipment failures and implement long-term corrective actions.
Maintain accurate asset registers, maintenance records, technical documentation, and spare-parts inventories.
Infrastructure Management
Oversee the operation and maintenance of critical systems, including:
Medium-voltage and low-voltage electrical distribution systems
Uninterruptible Power Supply systems and battery plants
Standby diesel generators
Automatic Transfer Switches
Switchgear, transformers, protection systems, and electrical panels
Chillers and chilled-water systems
Computer Room Air Handling and Computer Room Air Conditioning units
Air Handling Units
Pumps and hydronic systems
Heat exchangers
Building Management Systems
Data Center Infrastructure Management systems
Fire detection and suppression systems
Security and access-control systems
Fuel storage and distribution systems
Water-treatment and leak-detection systems
Health, Safety, Environmental and Regulatory Compliance
Ensure compliance with the French Labour Code, applicable EU directives, French environmental regulations, local requirements, and company policies.
Maintain a strong health, safety, and environmental culture across the facility.
Manage Permit to Work, Lockout/Tagout, electrical isolation, hot-work, confined-space, and contractor-safety programs.
Ensure employees and contractors hold the appropriate training, authorizations, and certifications for their assigned work.
Lead incident, near-miss, and equipment-failure investigations.
Conduct root-cause analysis and ensure corrective and preventive actions are completed.
Prepare for and support regulatory inspections, customer assessments, insurance reviews, and internal and external audits.
Ensure appropriate emergency-response plans, drills, and escalation procedures are maintained.
Capital Projects and Commissioning
Support the planning and delivery of infrastructure upgrades, replacements, expansions, and capital projects.
Review technical designs, specifications, risk assessments, and commissioning plans.
Coordinate project work with operations teams to minimize risk to live services.
Participate in factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, and integrated systems testing.
Ensure complete operational handover, including training, asset documentation, test results, warranties, and as-built drawings.
Monitor project budgets, schedules, risks, and contractor performance.
Financial and Vendor Management
Develop and manage the facilities operating and capital budgets.
Forecast maintenance, staffing, utility, equipment-replacement, and service-contract costs.
Review maintenance contracts, statements of work, and service-level agreements.
Monitor vendor performance against established service levels and key performance indicators.
Conduct regular vendor-performance reviews and implement improvement plans when required.
Support the procurement of equipment, spare parts, technical services, and facility-related contracts.
Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency without compromising safety, reliability, or compliance.
Sustainability and Energy Management
Identify and implement opportunities to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
Monitor Power Usage Effectiveness, energy consumption, water consumption, and carbon-related performance.
Support sustainability programs and environmental reporting requirements.
Work with engineering and operations teams to optimize cooling, electrical loading, and equipment performance.
Evaluate energy-saving initiatives while protecting system reliability and redundancy.

Riverside Park South is an award-winning waterfront park being constructed in six phases. Currently at 17 acres, it will eventually cover 32 acres, including a 750-foot pier, lawns, playgrounds, athletic fields, concessions and extensive horticulture.

The Park hosts significant free public programs funded by the Riverside South Property Owners Association through the Riverside Park Conservancy. · Under supervision, with latitude for independent initiative and judgment, perform assigned tasks to support the delivery of essential community services for Riverside Park South.

Communicate Park conditions, including public safety concerns, to appropriate Parks and Conservancy staff for resolution and aggressively pursue the immediate correction of safety hazards.

Work with Parks and Conservancy staff to establish and maintain a long-term horticultural maintenance plan. Maintain horticultural records and monitor plant materials purchased and installed throughout the park.
· Track maintenance and enforcement activities, programming, expenditures, work orders and inventory levels. Coordinate purchasing activities and oversee contractor services.
· Coordinate with Parks Enforcement and Maintenance & Operations (M&O) to ensure that public programming in Riverside Park South receives the necessary operational and enforcement support.
· Develop long-term strategies and plans for the effective maintenance and operation of Riverside Park South.
· Provide the Park Administrator and Riverside South Property Owners Association with regularly scheduled status reports regarding park operations, conditions and funding.
· Assist the Park Administrator with administrative responsibilities. Maintain accurate records, prepare comprehensive reports and respond to and track correspondence.
· Represent the Agency at meetings and serve as a liaison with the Riverside South Property Owners Association, Riverside Park Conservancy, other City agencies, institutions and community constituents.
